exam-11-q01.why_correct_en: St Helena and the Falkland Islands are British Overseas Territories: the UK is responsible for their sovereignty, but constitutionally they are not part of the UK. Eligible local residents are normally British Overseas Territories citizens (BOTCs) and may apply for the corresponding British passport. Since 21 May 2002, most BOTCs connected with these qualifying territories have also been British citizens; Falkland Islanders additionally benefited from the British Nationality (Falkland Islands) Act 1983. Many residents can therefore obtain a standard British citizen passport and may also hold a BOTC passport. BOTC status alone does not automatically give a right to live and work in the UK. Birth in a territory is not always sufficient by itself: the date of birth and a parent's citizenship or settled status also matter.

exam-11-q02.why_correct_en: London’s West End, also known as ‘Theatreland’, is particularly well known for its theatres.

exam-11-q03.why_correct_en: The currency in the UK is the pound sterling (symbol £).

exam-11-q09.why_correct_en: After the Norman Conquest, the king and his noblemen had spoken Norman French and the peasants had continued to speak Anglo-Saxon. Gradually these two languages combined to become one English language.

exam-11-q10.why_correct_en: UK broadcasters must observe due impartiality when covering political controversy and elections. This requires appropriate weight for significant rival viewpoints; it does not necessarily mean mechanically identical minutes for every party in every programme.

exam-11-q14.why_correct_en: In 1560, the predominantly Protestant Scottish Parliament abolished the authority of the Pope in Scotland and Roman Catholic religious services became illegal. A Protestant Church of Scotland with an elected leadership was established but, unlike in England, this was not a state Church.

exam-11-q15.why_correct_en: William the conqueror sent people all over England to draw up lists of all the towns and villages. The people who lived there, who owned the land and what animals they owned were also listed. This was called the Domesday Book, which gives a picture of society in England just after the Norman Conquest.

exam-11-q16.why_correct_en: The Northern Ireland Assembly can make decisions on issues such as: education, agriculture, the environment health and social services, but it cannot make decisions on immigration or defence issues.

exam-11-q17.why_correct_en: Anyone can make a complaint about the police by going to a police station and writing to the Chief Constable of the police force involved. Complaints can also be made to an independent body: the Independent Police Complaints Commission in England and Wales, the Police Complaints Commissioner for Scotland or the Police Ombudsman for Northern Ireland.

exam-11-q22.why_correct_en: Emmeline Pankhurst was born in Manchester in 1858. She set up the women’s Franchise League in 1889, which fought to get the vote in local elections for married women. In 1903 she helped found the Women’s Social and Political Union (WSPU). This was the first group whose members were called ‘suffragettes’.
